display.purpose: Page mastheads only — STOCK, Cars For Sale, the login wordmark. Never on /admin dashboard surfaces.

headline.purpose: The car title inside a register entry, and closing calls to action.

title.purpose: Subsection headings on the detail page.

body.purpose: Descriptive copy, capped at 68ch, always at the grey floor or lighter.

operate-title.purpose: Admin row car title. Sentence case, no display weight, no tracking.

shadows.name: panel-drop

motion.name: entry-rise
motion.purpose: The one authored animation: a register entry arriving. From an already-visible default; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Staggered index x 70ms, capped at 6.

motion.name: ease-register
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out; the system's only authored easing curve.

motion.name: hover-photo

motion.name: hover-rule
motion.purpose: The red bar growing along a register entry's top hairline.

motion.name: state-colour
motion.purpose: Default for button, link and border state changes. No transform, no lift.

narrative.overview:
This is a workshop's register, not a showroom and not a classifieds grid. Stock is set down as numbered lines under a rule: year, a locked photo crop, the car named at display scale, the preparation claim, the specs, the asking price. The structure does the persuading, because the photographs cannot — they are phone snaps taken on the lot, in mixed light, against a cluttered yard. A uniform photo-card grid would put every one of those snaps on trial. A ledger puts them in order, and order reads as competence.

The world is near-black, hard-edged and typographically loud. Poppins at black weight, uppercase, pulled tight (-0.045em), is the only ornament; a single red carries every signal there is. Nothing curves. There are no rounded corners, no gradients behind text, no soft cards floating on a wash — depth comes from one heavy offset shadow under the few elements that genuinely sit on top of the page, and from hairline rules everywhere else.

The system deliberately runs in two registers, and mixing them is the failure case. Persuade is the public surface: display type, hairlines, the red, the register structure. Operate is /admin: 14px semibold titles, 11.5px spec lines, ~60px rows, no display type and no marketing voice. The owner manages stock from a phone in the workshop; there, scanning speed beats expression, and the brand survives only in the accent and the square corners.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black grounds (#0a0f12 page, #111111 panel) and exactly one accent red
Zero border-radius on every rebuilt surface; square focus rings, square scrollbar, square icon caps
Hairline rules (1px #23292d) as the primary structural device, with a 2px red rule opening each register
Display-scale black uppercase Poppins at tracking -0.045em, against 11px uppercase labels at 0.18em — no middle ground
Tabular numerals on every price, km and year so columns never jitter
One authored animation, one shadow, one accent: the system's expressiveness is budgeted

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent hue in this system. A third hue (amber) was introduced during the build and removed in review. Red Pressed, Red Deep and Red Tint are states and fields of the same red, not siblings. The only non-red hue permitted anywhere is Live Green, and only on /admin.

rules.name: The Grey Floor Rule
rules.body: On #0a0f12, gray-700 (1.87:1), gray-600 (2.55:1) and gray-500 (3.99:1) all fail. gray-400 (#9ca3af, 7.59:1) is the lowest permissible grey for text. There is no grey between it and white in this system except gray-300.

rules.name: The No-Opacity-Recede Rule
rules.body: Never recede an element with opacity when its colour already sits at the grey floor — compositing drops it to roughly 2.5:1. Sold rows recede by switching white to gray-400 explicitly, and photos by desaturating. Opacity is permitted only on images, on disabled controls, and on a whole row mid-mutation.

rules.name: The Token Plumbing Rule
rules.body: Tailwind v4 here is CSS-first with no config file, and @theme inline inlines its values at each utility site — it never emits the custom properties, so hand-written CSS reading var(--color-signal) resolves empty and silently falls back to currentColor. A parallel plain :root block (--ink, --panel, --hairline, --signal) exists solely so the hand-written rules in globals.css can read the palette. Any new hand-written CSS uses the :root names; any new utility uses the @theme names. The legacy --color-primary: #FF9500 is orange, unused and misleading.

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Persuade and Operate never mix. Display-scale black uppercase type is forbidden on /admin (the login masthead is the single boundary marker); 14px semibold sentence-case titles are forbidden on public surfaces. If a new screen cannot say which register it is in, it is not designed yet.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No kicker, eyebrow or label line sits above a heading. The word carries its own weight; the masthead goes straight onto the page. Where a supporting line exists, it sits beside or below the heading, never above it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every price, kilometre figure and year carries .tnum (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums). These sit in columns across stacked rows and must not jitter between entries.

rules.name: The No-Uniform-Grid Rule
rules.body: Stock is never rendered as a grid of equal-sized cards. Entries are full-width lines separated by hairlines. Equipment lists and admin controls may use grids; stock may not.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is a single elevation step. An element either sits flat on the ground with a hairline, or it carries Panel Drop (0 30px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.8)). No intermediate shadows, no hover lift, no coloured glow.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: No rounded corners anywhere in the register language. The incumbent marketing sections carry pill-shaped CTAs (rounded-full); those are legacy surface, explicitly out of scope, and the radius does not propagate to any new work.

dos: Do state which register a new screen belongs to before designing it — Persuade (display type, red, hairlines, register structure) or Operate (14px semibold, 11.5px specs, ~60px rows).
Do open every register and every title band with the 2px Workshop Red rule, and separate every row with a 1px hairline.
Do keep body and supporting text at gray-400 (#9ca3af) or lighter on #0a0f12; recede elements with an explicit colour change, never with opacity.
Do put .tnum on every price, kilometre figure and year.
Do lock photo crops into fixed-aspect wells with object-cover, and desaturate at rest so a mismatched phone-photo set coheres.
Do serve images unoptimized through Cloudinary's own transform (w_800,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto at the needed width) and ship video preload="none" with a poster.
Do read palette values from the plain :root block (--ink, --panel, --hairline, --signal) in hand-written CSS, and from the @theme names in utilities.
Do theme the surfaces you did not draw: selection, scrollbar, tap highlight and focus ring all come from the palette.
Do animate arrivals with .entry-rise only — 0.62s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), from an already-visible default, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use a border-radius anywhere in the register language — not on buttons, inputs, badges, image wells, focus rings or active markers.
Don't render stock as a uniform grid of equal-sized photo cards; entries are full-width lines.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't introduce a third hue. Red Pressed, Red Deep and Red Tint are states of the one red; Live Green is scoped to the admin status indicator and appears nowhere public.
Don't use gray-500, gray-600 or gray-700 for text on #0a0f12 — all three fail contrast.
Don't write the focus-ring selector with :where(); zero specificity loses to preflight and Chrome's blue ring returns.
Don't read or extend --color-primary: #FF9500; it is orange, unused and misleading.
Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons, or import an icon package — extend the authored set at 24/1.75/square/miter.
Don't add a second shadow, a hover lift, or a coloured glow; Panel Drop is the only elevation step.
Don't let marketing voice, display type or persuasion copy into /admin.
